subject: Confirming 'no model training' commitments and snapshot retention mechanics
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@finovate.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Finovate Legal <legal@finovate.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question — 'we do not train' scope and backups

Sean — thanks for taking this early. We're working through the security questionnaire (attached) and Legal has two things they need clarified before we sign: 1) the scope of Redwood's 'we do not train on customer data' commitment (does this include fine-tuning, internal R&D, embeddings, k/v cache snapshots, logs?) and 2) the lifetime of any snapshots/backups/cold-archive that could ever contain customer text.

Specifically: can you confirm you never ingest customer content into model training pipelines or fine-tunes? If you do not, can you provide contract-friendly language and an operational illustration of retention windows for snapshots, backups, and telemetry so we can map that to our data-retention policy?

Attachment: security-questionnaire.pdf

Thanks,
Alice Park
Head of IT Security, Finovate Financial
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finovate.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question — 'we do not train' scope and backups

Alice — appreciate the clear asks. Short version up front: Redwood does not use customer content to train or fine-tune our public or internal models. We also do not add customer text to model-weight training datasets. There are a few operational telemetry and ephemeral artifacts used for service reliability (see below) — we can put contract language and a short addendum together.

High-level operational points:
- Model training: customer-provided content is not used for training or fine-tuning of models, nor for building foundation model datasets.
- Embeddings/derived vectors: we do not retain those for the purpose of improving models; they are treated as customer data and follow the retention rules below.
- KV/prefix cache & request caching: transient caches (KV cache, prefix cache) live in volatile memory during inference; when persisted for debug, those snapshots are stored only for troubleshooting and follow the retention windows below.
- Telemetry/ops logs: we collect aggregated telemetry for performance and billing (latency buckets, token counts). Full request payloads are not retained except for a limited troubleshooting window.

We're drafting contract language (attached: redwood-no-train-addendum.docx) that: 1) commits to 'no training on customer text', 2) defines retention windows for troubleshooting snapshots and backups, and 3) lays out an erase flow. Priyom / Irene — can you review the addendum & the retention bullets below for technical/legal completeness?

Thanks,
Sean
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Park <alice.park@finovate.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Finovate Legal <legal@finovate.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question — 'we do not train' scope and backups

Thanks Sean — that helps. A few follow-ups from Legal and our InfoSec team:
1) Snapshots: can you confirm whether snapshots/backups ever enter immutable cold storage (e.g., an object store with lifecycle rules) and what the maximum retention period is? We typically ask for a 30-day deletion guarantee for live copies and a 90-day max for backups unless there's a legal hold.
2) Evidence: can you provide an example audit extract (redacted) showing deletion events or a sample export of logs that demonstrates deletion propagation? Even a sanitized CSV or a secure Drive link is useful.

If you can commit contractually to the 30/90 windows (with standard legal-hold carveouts) that would close most of our concerns.

Alice
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finovate.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question — 'we do not train' scope and backups (technical details)

Hi Alice — technical clarifications below. I'm on the infra side and handle data lifecycle for Redwood's hosted offering. Short answers and then specifics: yes, we can commit to a 30-day deletion SLA for live/primary copies and a 90-day maximum for backups/cold-archives absent legal hold; we also support an export + confirm delete workflow.

Details:
- Live request data: by default, full request payloads are retained for troubleshooting for up to 14 days (configurable per-customer, default 14). After that they are purged from hot stores.
- Diagnostic snapshots: we occasionally persist sanitized snapshots (traces plus minimal request context) to object storage for post-mortem and bug fixes. These are TTL'd and deleted automatically — default TTL 30 days; can be contract-bound to 30 days.
- Immutable backups/cold-archive: backups are created daily and retained in cold object storage for up to 90 days for restore scenarios. Backups are encrypted at rest (customer KMS optional). Backups are covered by our standard backup lifecycle and can be contractually limited to 90 days except for legal holds.
- Deletion propagation: delete requests trigger a multi-stage workflow: mark-for-delete -> background scrub -> metadata tombstone -> physical removal from hot/persistent stores. We also rotate keys for customer-specific KMS scopes which ensures orphaned encrypted blobs become inaccessible after key destruction (subject to mutual agreement on key custody).
- Audit/export: we can generate a redacted audit extract showing deletion timestamps and object keys; we typically deliver via a signed, expiring S3/Drive link.

Operational exceptions:
- Legal hold: if Finovate issues a preservation notice, standard carveouts apply.
- Backups in third-party regions: we can restrict backup replication by region if required by residency constraints.

I'll attach a short diagram and example commands in the addendum. Happy to walk through on a technical call.

Cheers,
Priyom
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finovate.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question — 'we do not train' scope and backups (privacy/legal wording)

Alice — adding suggested contract wording and a checklist for your counsel. Feel free to copy/modify. Key points to include: 1) "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any models, and will not incorporate Customer Content into model training datasets;" 2) "Redwood will retain live request data for troubleshooting for no longer than 30 days and backups for no longer than 90 days, except as required by legal hold;" 3) "Upon Customer request Redwood will provide an export of customer data and confirm deletion within 30 days for live stores and indicate expected removal date from backups (within 90 days)."

Evidence path: our SOC2 auditor can produce a redacted extract of deletion events and our security team can provide a snapshot of retention lifecycle policies (see Drive link below). We can bundle that as an "audit evidence" zip.

Suggested link for evidence (sanitized): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/EXAMPLE-AUDIT

Best,
Irene Choi
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finovate.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Finovate Legal <legal@finovate.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question — 'we do not train' scope and backups (next steps)

Alice — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Attached are: 1) redwood-no-train-addendum.docx (proposed contractual language, includes the 30/90 retention commitments and legal-hold carveout) and 2) a small bundle of redacted audit extracts (audit-extracts.zip) showing deletion-event samples.

If the addendum looks good to Legal, I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute call with Priyom (infra) and Irene (privacy) to walk the evidence and sign off. Proposed windows we agree to:
- Live stores / troubleshooting snapshots: 30 days
- Backups / cold-archive: 90 days max
- Legal hold: standard carveout

Please let me know a time for a call or if Legal would like a minor edit to the addendum.

Best,
Sean
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-no-train-addendum.docx, audit-extracts.zip
